text:
lucas: FYI we pushed kernel-routing change A -> noticed host-side p95 jump on streaming/chat-short. dropping quick notes.

lucas: baseline host-parse p95: 190ms -> after-change: 320ms. QPS same, throughput -4%.

neha: any perf flame?

lucas: quick perf sample diffs:
```
memcpy           3%  -> 18%
parse_tokenize   15% -> 28%
writev/syscalls  4%  -> 12%
kv_cache_lookup  9%  -> 8%
```

arya: writev/syscalls up suggests more, smaller syscalls from ingress. Did we change streaming chunking or pre-serialize per-request?

lucas: We started doing a per-request linearize+probe to estimate packed size to pick the "packed_fast" kernel pre-batch. That does a small memcpy and then calls write path when reply is streamed. For many tiny requests we're now paying two copies + more syscalls.

neha: So double-copy: probe linearize, then batcher merges -> another copy to batch buffer. Plus more writev frames. Bad for tail.

ops-bot: Canary CI quick metrics:
- host-parse CPU: +14%
- small-chat p95: +65%
- syscall rate (writev/readv): +220%
- allocs/sec: +28%

arya: Short triage plan: 1) rollback selector change on canary 2) implement ingress coalescer (coalesce small gRPC chunks into a single writev up to 8KB) 3) add a per-worker scratch pool for probe linearize to avoid heap allocs 4) experiment with making kernel selection post-batch.

neha: Agree. Also add telemetry tags: kernel_selection={prebatch,postbatch}, probe_linearize=true/false, scratch_pool_hit=true/false, ingress_coalesce=true/false, syscall_count. We need to see where syscalls are coming from.

lucas: I'll open quick revert PR and a sticky-scratch PR behind a flag. PRs: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/2567 (revert) and https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/2568 (scratch pool).

arya: For coalescer, prototype in ingress path: buffer up to N small stream chunks or 2ms, then emit a single writev. Should reduce syscall tail. Label as feature flag ingress.coalesce.

neha: Microbench matrix to run after revert: A) baseline B) bad-canary C) scratch-pool D) scratch+coalesce E) postbatch-select (if ready). We'll measure p50/p95, mem allocs, syscall counts, memcpy time, kvcache hit-rate.

lucas: One more caveat: kvcache keying. If probe normalizes bytes (trim, unicode normalize), keys might shift. Keep probe as raw-copy only; do not change canonical bytes. Add kvcache_key_source tag.

bench-bot: microbench queued: rt-replay/355555-1 with configs A..E. ETA ~45m.

ops-bot: Revert deployed to canary at 13:02 UTC. Monitoring.

lucas: Post-revert quick numbers (13:20): memcpy % in sample down to 4%, syscall rate back to baseline, host-parse p95 198ms. Revert fixed immediate perf regression.

arya: Nice. Next: land scratch-pool and coalescer behind flags. Sticky pool design: per-worker ring of fixed buffers (8x8KB), no heap alloc on hit, metric scratch_pool_hit_rate. If pool miss, fall back to malloc and tag.

neha: For post-batch selection: we need batch metadata that contains per-request fragment descriptors so kernel can decide on iov vs packed kernels without per-request preprobe. That is a slightly larger refactor (kernel+batcher). Put on roadmap: RTX-5333 (kernel iov/segment support).

lucas: I'll attach the perf flame and the small repro script to RTX-5333 and to the PRs. I'll also add dashboard panels for syscall counts and ingress coalesce hit rate.

bench-bot: scratch-pool PR perf quickcheck: allocs/sec -78% vs bad-canary, memcpy portion -60% vs bad-canary. Full replay pending.

neha: If scratch-pool + ingress coalesce lift the tail, we can keep prebatch heuristics but gate them with ingress.coalesce=true or probe_mode=sticky. Otherwise postpone selector until after batching.

arya: Also watch for corner cases: HTTP clients that stream many tiny frames with long pauses; coalescer timeout must be short to avoid added latency. Start with 2ms coalesce window and test for p50 impact.

lucas: TL;DR: quick rollback done; landing scratch pool + ingress coalescer experiments behind flags; long-term kernel iov support. Will post microbench results here.

neha: Thanks, quick detection+rollback as usual. Keep updates in RTX-5333 and tag perf dashboards.

arya: Adding flame screenshot to RTX-5333 now.
